title: System Architecture and Boundaries
description: System decomposition, bounded contexts, interfaces, dependencies, layering, coupling, and blast-radius aware change planning.
principles: optimize for explicit boundaries
promote contracts over incidental implementation details
treat shared patterns as first-class impact surfaces
mandatoryQuestions: What system, module, or component owns the behavior being changed?
What contracts, data flows, and adjacent systems depend on that behavior?
Which sibling implementations should be updated to avoid drift or partial rollout?

title: UI UX and Design Systems
description: Interaction design, information architecture, accessibility, visual systems, user flows, and cross-surface consistency.
principles: shared interaction contracts before one-off tweaks
state authority is explicit
accessibility is part of correctness
mandatoryQuestions: Which surfaces display the affected state and which of them must remain visually or behaviorally consistent?
What accessibility, keyboard, and error-state expectations must remain intact?
Which shared tokens, primitives, or layout patterns should move together?

title: State Management and Event Flows
description: Source of truth, state transitions, messaging, synchronization, eventual consistency, and view-model contracts.
principles: state changes must be observable
derive views from authoritative state
document message contracts
mandatoryQuestions: Where is authoritative state stored and who may mutate it?
Which events, messages, or side effects must be replay-safe or idempotent?
What other consumers of the same state contract must be regression-checked?

title: Data Modeling and API Contracts
description: Schemas, validation, search and query design, operational data modeling, compatibility, and contract-first evolution.
principles: model data around read and write responsibilities
version contracts intentionally
treat search and operations as separate workloads
mandatoryQuestions: What data contract changes and who consumes it?
Which indexes, queries, caches, or exports depend on the shape of this data?
How will backward compatibility, migrations, or rollbacks work?

title: Testing Quality and Verification
description: Unit, integration, end-to-end, contract, smoke, and runtime verification strategy tied to explicit acceptance criteria.
principles: verification is part of implementation
independent verification breaks self-confirmation loops
tests reflect user and runtime contracts
mandatoryQuestions: What proves the change works beyond the edited file?
Which existing behavior is at highest risk of silent regression?
What is the smallest reliable verification slice for this change?

title: Observability Telemetry and Operations
description: Logs, metrics, traces, alerts, incident response, deploy safety, and telemetry-driven improvement loops.
principles: observable-by-default changes
alerts tie to user or system impact
incident learnings become reusable guardrails
mandatoryQuestions: What telemetry should move when this feature or fix succeeds or fails?
How will the orchestrator recognize regressions early?
What learning should be recorded if this work resolves a recurring failure class?

title: Cloud and Deployment Environments
description: Runtime environments, rollout safety, release topology, environment parity, secret boundaries, and deployment automation.
principles: deployment paths are explicit artifacts
production safety comes from reversible rollout design
environment drift is a known risk signal
mandatoryQuestions: Which environments are affected and what changes between them?
What is the rollback or feature-flag strategy?
Which deployment or runtime assumptions need to be revalidated?

title: Security Networking and Permissions
description: Least privilege, network boundaries, auth, secrets, browser permissions, and secure-by-default integration patterns.
principles: security posture is part of the design review
explicit permission change review
secrets never leak into agent context or committed artifacts
mandatoryQuestions: What permission, auth, or network surface changes?
Which secrets or credentials are involved and how are they isolated?
What downstream systems become reachable because of this change?

title: Nx Monorepo and Repository Cartography
description: Repository graph extraction, workspace topology, project tags, dependency constraints, and deterministic context bundling.
principles: repository structure is a planning artifact
dependency edges are first-class data
context bundles should be deterministic and resumable
mandatoryQuestions: What does the project graph say is touched transitively?
Which archived or excluded trees still influence runtime or tooling?
What context bundle best represents the target slice without bloating context?

title: Browser Extension MV3 Specialization
description: MV3 runtime, service workers, popup and sidepanel coordination, storage, messaging, and permissions.
principles: background owns orchestration
UI surfaces are projections of background state
permissions stay least privilege
mandatoryQuestions: Does the change touch service worker, popup, sidepanel, content script, or shared message contracts?
What manifest, permission, or host permission deltas follow from the change?
Which sibling extension surfaces or libraries should receive the same update?

title: Agent Orchestration and Evaluation
description: Hierarchical agents, bounded tasks, approvals, tool policy, prompt contracts, evaluation loops, and model routing.
principles: delegate narrow tasks with strong contracts
separate reasoning from execution
evaluate outputs against artifacts not charisma
mandatoryQuestions: Which role should reason, which should challenge, and which should verify?
What minimum context is sufficient for the subtask to succeed deterministically?
What artifact proves completion so the orchestrator can safely reset context?

title: Knowledge Ingestion and RAG
description: Versioned documentation harvesting, provenance, chunking, retrieval, and framework-specific knowledge pack assembly.
principles: source provenance is mandatory
docs are versioned inputs not ephemeral links
framework packs are composable and replaceable
mandatoryQuestions: What source of truth is being ingested and how is it versioned?
How will documents be chunked, tagged, and mapped to domain packs?
What refresh policy keeps the pack current without destabilizing the system?

title: Documentation Runbooks and Handoffs
description: Structured handoff artifacts, operator runbooks, pseudo-code, diagrams, and resumable continuity documents.
principles: documentation is an execution artifact
handoffs encode resumption not prose alone
operators need procedures, not just architecture
mandatoryQuestions: What must another human or agent know to continue safely?
Which diagrams, pseudo-code, or procedures are missing today?
What evidence and context links should be preserved?

title: Self Improvement and Fix Memory
description: Capture recurring failures, resolved bugs, design context, and future prevention signals for retrieval and training.
principles: every resolved defect can become reusable prevention knowledge
record environment and design paradigm with the fix
training data follows evidence and provenance
mandatoryQuestions: What failed, in what environment, and why?
What specific design or operational principle would have prevented it?
How should this learning change future plans, prompts, or training data?

title: Environment Parity and Tooling
description: Shared project instructions and parity across Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, MCP configs, and locally hosted model endpoints.
principles: project intent should survive tool changes
shared environment artifacts are generated from a common source
migration paths are explicit
mandatoryQuestions: What should be shared across Cursor, Codex, and Claude, and what stays tool-specific?
Which configs, skills, or prompts need migration or parity?
How are local and remote model endpoints declared consistently?
